# HISTORY — the shape of the `mjc` node

*Auto-generated big-picture history. Overwrite freely; do not hand-edit narrative into it.*
*Window covered: 2026-07-22 through 2026-07-31 (this node's entire life so far — ~50 commits, ~10 days).*

## Why this node exists

`mjc` was founded to fill a missing rung on the substrate ladder: something between RHM (symbolic, known-latent) and language — continuous, contact-rich dynamics, but still a **DGP whose knobs we set and sweep**, never an RL-to-SOTA benchmark. The founding doc, [`ideas/physical_control_substrate.md`](../../ideas/physical_control_substrate.md), was prompted by asking where vanilla scaling+imitation robot policies are structurally confounded, and pitched five payoffs: physical arity, a free perfect-simulator oracle, contact as a physically-real residual test, an on-demand lossy channel (dynamics shift), and — most ambitiously — **drift as a novelty generator** that should force a forward model (FM) to grow new representational capacity. Two of these five founding bets were later run and explicitly retracted; tracing why is most of this history.

## Era 1 — the three foundational cuts (2026-07-22 to ~07-24)

Cut #1 ([`contact_residual/`](contact_residual/README.md)) set out to check whether "residual = surprise, scales with DGP complexity" survives real contact physics. The naive prediction — contact residual should just be *bigger* — was true but shallow; the sharper, load-bearing finding only appeared after switching to an onset-aligned event-triggered average: the residual **spikes at the impact transition and decays while contact persists**, marking a residual as an **event/regime-transition detector, not a state detector**. A methodological gotcha (plain MSE collapses the contrast; Huber loss is required) became a standing convention.

Cut #2 ([`arity_torque/`](arity_torque/README.md)) transplanted the arity-2-beats-arity-1 result onto a real actuator, deliberately killing the "command derivable from state" confound with i.i.d. commands (max|corr(u,s)|=0.003). The result reproduced almost embarrassingly cleanly (arity-2 R²≈0.999 at every capacity; arity-1 flat at ~0) — notable less for surprise than for how load-bearing its i.i.d.-command premise would turn out to be later (Era 4 shows this premise is a **teleport-only luxury**).

Cut #3 ([`dynamics_shift/`](dynamics_shift/README.md)) is where the founding doc's flagship idea — a static "degradation slope" under dynamics shift — was explicitly judged theoretically shaky mid-cut and **replaced** with a sharper, MuJoCo-unique claim: a shifted transition operator corrupts only the world-model factor, so a model-based agent recovers from ~50 reward-free transitions while a matched model-free policy needs ~240× more *reward-labeled* data. This only worked once the team diagnosed that per-step replanning was substituting for a stale model and swapped to committed, open-loop control (the `replan_every` ablation) — establishing **commitment horizon** as a causal knob that essentially every later node reuses. Cut #3 is explicitly named "the substrate most later nodes build on."

## Era 2 — value-shaping, then the phenomenon-first pivot (~07-24 to 07-26)

[`value_shaping/`](value_shaping/README.md) asked whether a value signal causes an FM to reallocate scarce capacity toward value-relevant dynamics. Two design failures preceded the working version: a high-energy-but-linear puck gave nothing to reallocate ("energy ≠ prediction cost"), and the genuinely hard part of the physics (contact) is *irreducible* per Cut #1, so it can't be the thing dropped. The fix — an engineered, deterministic, capacity-hungry-but-reducible force field — produced a robust re-allocation result, but the hoped-for capacity-*efficiency* "teeth" were honestly reported as a fragile, data-scarcity artifact. This node was deliberately built as the **stationary control** for everything non-stationary that follows.

[`directed_readapt/`](directed_readapt/README.md) then asked the natural next question — does a value/uncertainty-*directed* drive beat undirected re-adaptation? — and returned two clean negatives: a global shift needs no direction (no scarcity to exploit), and, more importantly, a **localized** shift breaks disagreement as a targeting signal, because an ensemble warm-started from a stale prior *agrees* on its wrong prediction inside the unvisited region. This produced the arc's first durable mechanistic lesson (disagreement flags uncertainty, not confident-wrongness) and an explicit strategic pivot: stop verifying isolated mechanistic atoms one at a time, and build the actual compounding-adaptation *phenomenon* first, back-translating mechanism from what works.

[`meta_adapt/`](meta_adapt/README.md) (#4→#4e) executed that pivot and became the arc's central spine. It reproduced RHM's collapse result on a too-shared task family (meta ≈ multitask, gap≈0), then found the gap opens **monotonically with task conflict** (an actuator-rotation family, up to 8× at Φ=π/2) — establishing *conflict*, not mere non-stationarity, as the precondition for meta-learning to earn its keep. An explicit context latent `z` (#4b) then produced the arc's recurring dissociation, replayed in every later node: **you can perfectly identify a task and that identification can be worthless** (system-ID ⊥ adaptation-benefit), a result the team calls "true but useless." #4c reconfirmed this for value-directed *exploration* (VoI-directed identification is a robust negative — magnitude-based collection wins "for free" on a 1-D system-ID problem). #4d/#4e transposed the same dissociation onto the FM/value-shaping side and closed the loop with a fully reward-driven outer loop, surfacing a reusable wireheading gotcha (an unconstrained per-dim weight games loss *scale*, not allocation — fixed by normalizing to a softmax budget).

[`curiosity_control/`](curiosity_control/README.md) closed the explore-side half of the interface, transplanting an RPF-ensemble fix onto a genuinely *drifting* frontier. It reconfirmed the tracking-vs-usefulness dissociation on the explore side and delivered the era's sharpest negative: pure curiosity is **seduced by a noisy TV** on this low-dimensional substrate — an explicit *inversion* of an earlier high-dimensional active-vision result, because low-dim ensembles fit distinct noise realizations instead of converging past it. The resolution — ground explore with an *additive* value term rather than filtering it — is the belief state the era ends on: explore and exploit are one coupled two-tap system, gated by conflict, capacity, and non-stationarity.

## Era 3 — the two-timescale loop, obstructed twice, resolved by re-grading (~07-26 to 07-27)

[`online_value_loop/`](online_value_loop/README.md) tried to make both taps (explore/exploit balance, FM capacity allocation) tune themselves *live*, online, in a single loop — and both were obstructed, for different reasons: CEM-MPC replanning is simply robust to the explore drive's tracking effect, and the value-shaping benefit washes out once the FM converges (a short-enough probe to see it degenerates into a full retrain). The team reframed this negative as **confirmation, not failure**: value is forced onto the slow/committed timescale by the structure of the problem, and its payoff is *adaptation speed*, not converged competence — which only matters under perpetual, never-converging drift.

[`drift_value_loop/`](drift_value_loop/README.md) tested exactly that and found a second-order surprise: compounding across a drift sequence is real and dramatic, but it comes from the **memory architecture** (a context-latent FM), not from value-carving — which stayed capacity-gated and control-robust, replaying #4d's null. Rather than stopping there, the team diagnosed *why*: reward is a **near-blind grader** of FM quality. Re-grading the meta-loop by value-relevant **FM prediction error** instead of downstream reward — the literal cerebellum→VTA analogy — gave the explore/exploit balance a clean interior optimum where control stayed dead flat. The lesson, stated explicitly: the missing piece was never the value *structure*, it was the *teacher*.

[`ballistic/`](ballistic/README.md) built the genuinely non-re-groundable controller `drift_value_loop` had named as its own next step, to test whether FM quality transmits to behavior once replanning can't paper over it. A first attempt (4a) was a diagnosed negative (explore/exploit roles had inverted on this geometry, so the intended axis was never varied); once that confound was removed, feedforward/ballistic control transmitted FM quality **~3×** more than reactive, and reward-free re-adaptation restored ballistic competence **~4.3×** more after a drift. This reframed the "blind grader" problem a third time — not as a fact about value, but about **control mode** — and produced the era's headline synthesis: the FM is simultaneously the one motor asset maintainable *without* reward and the asset feedforward control depends on. Same object.

[`ballistic/directed/`](ballistic/directed/README.md) closed the loop mechanically (relevance × reducibility recovers the oracle allocation one-shot; ensemble disagreement provably cannot detect staleness, only missing data) but then produced this era's most self-aware moment: an online-loop result ("relevance doesn't pay in a loop," S2) was **retracted on audit** — traced to reusing the exact blind-grader pathology `drift_value_loop` had already diagnosed, plus metric contamination and a **22× measurement subsidy** from free, unmetered monitoring. The corrected status was downgraded from *falsified* to *untested*, with an explicit methodological rule drawn: never read a program-level belief downgrade off an instrument you've already shown to be blind. This retraction is the direct seed of Era 4.

## Era 4 — the realism audit: acquisition, physics, and a founding motivation retired (~07-27 to 07-31, the live thread)

[`on_policy/COLLECTION_REALISM.md`](on_policy/COLLECTION_REALISM.md) named the node's standing unrealism directly: every FM had trained on **teleported** transitions (`set_state` + arbitrary command) — free, omniscient, discontinuous. Rather than reject teleport, the memo stratified its damage into three tiers (safe dissociations; inflated absolute sample counts; **unaskable** allocation-of-experience questions — exactly the class the `ballistic/directed` S2 audit fell into) and proposed a single reversible flag, `collection_mode`, on the existing envs, with `embodied.py`'s metered `Body` making `set_state` structurally unavailable rather than merely discouraged.

Building and pricing that flag ([`on_policy/`](on_policy/README.md), E0–E2) falsified the memo's own working hypotheses twice in a row. E0: most of on-policy's apparent efficiency edge was a **mistuned teleport default**, not embodiment — what's genuinely structural is command-state entanglement from continuity itself, retroactively marking Cut #2's clean i.i.d.-command premise as a teleport-only luxury. E1: the memo's headline prediction (embodiment should stretch a step-like recovery into a graded curve) was **refuted** — under global drift, embodiment is nearly free. Only E2, by deliberately localizing the drift, found the real cost: on-policy needs 2.5× more transitions, because a stale model produces wrong-distributed data while it's learning — not "coverage grows," the humbler mechanism that survived the test.

That local-drift regime is what makes "where should I practise?" askable again — the exact claim `ballistic/directed` had retracted. [`on_policy/directed_on_policy/`](on_policy/directed_on_policy/README.md) (E3) delivered it once looking itself is metered (a 1.84× ratio, not 22×): both retracted halves reproduce, relevance and reducibility-awareness both pay, matching a privileged oracle. [`on_policy/metered_repair/`](on_policy/metered_repair/README.md) (E4/E5) is the thread still live at window's end: E4 lands a genuine positive (a visited-but-irreducible cell makes relevance-alone the *worst* arm, and the conjunction beats it decisively) alongside two honest nulls — a ported repair mechanism that diagnoses correctly but doesn't cash out, and a hand-built rate-vs-level hypothesis the data simply does not support. E5 extends the same discipline to a necessity question and returns a clean null: on a fixed-DOF plant, repairing one region does not repair another, because the FM has no route to shared-parameter inference — directly reusing Era-4's own instrumentation.

In parallel, [`arm_substrate/`](arm_substrate/README.md) opened a second, *orthogonal* realism axis — physics/task-family diversity, not acquisition — replacing the pusher's manufactured capacity competition with one intrinsic to a nonlinear plant (binds only at chain length ≥5), and reproducing the ballistic/reactive asymmetry with a genuinely new readout (a mirror-signed aftereffect the pusher can't produce). Its README is explicit that this axis is independent of acquisition realism, and that any directed-collection cut ported onto the arm needs on-policy collection first — the clearest statement in the node that realism is several independent dials, not one.

## The parallel closure — Cut #5, expansion (07-27)

[`expansion/`](expansion/README.md) finally ran the founding doc's most ambitious, longest-deferred bet: does drift on a fixed-DOF plant open the FM's representational frontier? Using a three-piece calibrate→measure→calibrate design (needed because rank-shaped instruments had failed here three times before), it found drift moves the frontier by only **±0.08 directions**, ~10× below a **+0.72±0.42** calibration from a genuine capacity increase (unlocking real joints). This **closed the founding bet**: drift moves the target function; only adding genuine degrees of freedom expands the space of representable functions. [`ideas/physical_control_substrate.md`](../../ideas/physical_control_substrate.md) itself was edited to mark this extension "Retired 2026-07-27," while explicitly preserving drift's *other* role — realism — which the entire `drift_value_loop`/`on_policy` line still depends on. The instrument built to close it (`R_res_participation`/frontier mass) outlived the cut and is reused directly by `metered_repair`'s E5.

## Where belief stands at the end of this window

The node's throughline is a repeated pattern: state a hypothesis sharp enough to fail, build the instrument that could refute it, and when it does fail, ask whether the *structure* was wrong or the *grader* was blind — "the teacher, not the value" (`drift_value_loop`), "the control mode, not the value" (`ballistic`), "the subsidy, not the relevance" (`ballistic/directed`), "the knob, not the embodiment" (`on_policy`). Two founding bets from the idea doc were tested and explicitly retracted (the degradation-slope framing in Cut #3; drift-as-novelty-generator in `expansion/`) without weakening the program — each retraction sharpened the surviving claim. The live thread at window's end is [`on_policy/metered_repair/`](on_policy/metered_repair/README.md)'s necessity/repair-mechanism work, and per [`README.md`](README.md)'s own "Next steps," the standing open question is whether ensemble disagreement — shown structurally blind to staleness in `ballistic/directed` — recovers its job once on-policy collection creates territory that is genuinely, rather than nominally, unvisited.
